chapters.title: Chapter 436: Killing The Assassins
paragraphs: When Kent left the carriage, Lady Lani and Nara also left and appeared a few meters away.

It was the only way for Nara to keep an eye on him and perhaps help him if he got in over his head. It was her way of doing her job as his guard and seeing if he could wield the sword like how he could handle his women.
Though he rescued her from captivity, she still wants to see him in action.
After watching him kill the first assassin, they followed him to the place where the rest were hidden. It was a weird thing to do, but they followed him.
Naturally, Lady Lani knew if she were in Kent’s place, she would sneak in and eliminate them individually. Nara would have done the same.
But not Kent.
The bastard walked to the front door and stopped.
"What is he coming to do?" Nara asked. "I can count five Ascension-stage cultivators in there and ten Transcendents. He wouldn’t actually kick his way in."
"If he were able to fight against Evil Bat, who is a Sovereign, then he would do just that."
As if he were waiting for that cue from Lady Lani, Kent kicked the door in and walked inside, wiping the dust off his sleeves.
He was immediately surrounded.
Then, to their shock, he actually decided to drop one wise saying.
Nara looked at Lady Lani’s face as if to say, "This motherfucker didn’t just do that."
But Kent just stood there, and after dropping the icy saying on them, he gave them that classic line.
"Gentlemen, shall we?"
His sword appeared in his hand as one of the Transcendents lunged at him with daggers drawn. Kent stepped backward, evading the attack like it was the easiest thing a person could do.
This stunned the assassin.
Then his sword came out of the sheath and went back in, along with the head of the assassin falling to the ground.
It was one quick and precise draw that happened so quickly. After the head fell, the assassins knew the monster before them could not be killed.
The assassin he killed was one of their best, so the moment his classic one-dash kill attack failed, they knew they had to run.
"Oh, but you cannot run," Kent smiled and activated one of the abilities unlocked when he upgraded the [Soul Shock] skill.
"Soul Lock." The entire space around the house where the assassins were hiding was locked down. "No running now unless you want to die the most painful way."
His warning was heard by all, and like he said, none of them moved, for they knew they were under rather powerful soul energy.
Those closer to the boundaries of the soul lock felt their souls getting pressed down hard.
"Kill him," one of the Ascension-stage assassins ordered, and like the obedient assassins they were, they lunged at Kent.
He moved back, evading an arrow aimed at his head. In return, he turned and locked eyes with the assassin atop a structure who was using the crossbow against him.
His eyes shone, and the assassin who locked eyes with him fell from the structure to his death.
’Fuck, that was dangerous.’
Kent used the [Soul Rending Glare] for the first time, and it was more lethal than he expected.

⟪The person has no defenses around their soul nor any treasure protecting their soul, so it was a direct attack. But even if their soul is protected, you are a Tier 10 soul cultivator; killing him was a normal thing to do.⟫
Akira said to Kent, making him smile as he dodged yet another arrow from the second bowman. He used the Soul Rending Glare again, and the results were the same.
The assassin fell to his death, making Kent sigh. Then he pulled his sword from the sheath and unleashed his Level 9 Enhanced Sword Intent and Qi.
He moved and executed a series of sword attacks, creating sword lights in the air. They all happened very fast and were over before they knew it.
He arrived back at the position he had moved from, and when he sheathed his sword again, all the Transcendents there were beheaded.
It was as simple as unleashing an attack, and like he expected, they all died.
Kent glared at the Ascension-stage assassins who were looking around themselves, watching the headless bodies of their teammates on the ground.
Kent didn’t bother with that. Instead, he acted with two skills.
The void cracked behind them, and two crescent sword arcs flashed out, cutting four in half. It was a quick, precise attack that came and went like the wind.
Perhaps it was because of shock, or because assassins naturally lack stronger defense, or maybe both, but killing four Level 2 Ascension-stage assassins that quickly shouldn’t be that simple.
Yet on the ground now were the four who died before even the void closed.
The only one left was the leader, who was at the 4th level of the Root Ascension stage. His sword vanished, and he glared at the clearly terrified assassin.
"I planted a soul bomb into your soul, so your death is going to be as simple as snapping my finger. However, you still have a chance to live after this.
So answer my questions well and perhaps I will be generous."
Kent spoke coldly to the assassin, whose grip on his dagger loosened, and the dagger fell to the ground. The battle happened in under two minutes.
The brat he and his men were bragging about capturing and torturing before killing had broken through their front door and killed every last one of them, leaving only him.
And now, even though it sounded unbelievable, he is hearing that there is a bomb planted in his heart.
In truth, Kent was telling the truth.
After upgrading the [Soul Shock] skill to the Mystical grade, its name changed to [Soul Mapping Arts].

It became something akin to a technique with multiple skills. The description described these as abilities; the first ability was the [Soul Brand] he used on the Assassin he spotted during the alchemy trial and later used to locate him.
The second was the [Soul Lock] skill, which locks the space around 50 meters. If not allowed by him, anything that tries to get in or out experiences an agonizing soul attack.
If not strong enough in the soul, they will die.
The last skill is called [Soul Bomb]. This can only be used once every two hours. It basically turns one’s soul into a bomb with a casual snap of his finger as the detonator.
So he wasn’t bluffing.

"We will meet soon enough," he said before destroying the mark.

"Kent Madson."
The gritting of his teeth could be heard many miles away.

chapters.title: Chapter 437: Just How Old Are You?
paragraphs: Inside a large castle, or so it appeared considering its bath in countless formations, a being with a twisted expression was sitting in a lotus posture, eyes closed, as if meditating.
The air around him reeked of death, showing he had killed his fair share of people, and because of that, he now exuded the aura of a killer.
Suddenly, his eyes snapped open, and blood came out of them.
His mouth and nose weren’t spared either. This brought him intense pain, one that made him twist his expression as if he had been struck by a truck.
"Kent Madson."
He gritted his teeth, saying that.
"I will kill you." His tone was dull and cold, showing how determined he was.
He was a Level 8 Sovereign and the leader of one of the most elite yet dangerous assassin organizations on the human continent.
Just now, an affiliate of his organization, the Grim Brothers assassin unit, had been murdered. He knew that simply because of the soul marks he left on them vanished.
He had those on all his men.
So the moment they died, he became aware. But that was his plan all along. He had planned to send them to their death since he never really expected them to be able to kill Kent.
His main attack was the soul attack he used to kill the leader who was about to divulge all he knew about his employer.
While killing him was a way to keep his identity safe, his aim was Kent. He had planned to use the soul attack on him.
It was a soul talisman skill at the 7th tier he had procured at an auction. All he had to do was plant it on his subordinate, and it would have done its work.
Not that it would have worked on Kent, considering he was immune to soul attacks. But even without that, he was a Tier 10 soul cultivator. Killing him with a Tier 7 soul skill was just plain stupid.
Unfortunately for him, Kent got hold of the talisman, which contained a trace of his soul energy. He couldn’t kill him, so he used his soul to destroy it, and in doing so, the figure was struck hard.
He might be a Sovereign, but his soul was only Tier 7. Though his cultivation base could compensate for the rest, killing someone in the 10th tier was indeed foolish.
The moment he recovered from the attack, he left the room he was in and appeared in a large hall where seven hooded figures were seated.
Each reeked of death and was between Level 1 and Level 5 Root Sovereign stages. The figure walked closer to the head chair and sat down.
"How did it go, Leader?" one of the seven asked.
"He survived, but not for long." His tone was cold as usual. He then asked, "Have you started making preparations?"

"Yes, Leader. Vastport City is surrounded, and the formations are in place," one of them answered. "Also, there are reports that some people are already in place and after the same brat. Should we eliminate them?"
"Eliminate those that will cross our mission. Kent Madson must die before the week ends. Remember who gave us this mission and know that failure is not an option."
"Okay, Leader."

"Also, send word to the Evil Sects. I learned that their previous sect master is out for blood. Let them know that in four days’ time, the brat who caused them to close their doors will be trapped in Vastport City."
"Okay, Leader."
The seven figures melded into the shadows and left the hall. The Sovereign let out a heavy sigh and departed, leaving the hall empty.
Kent knew nothing of this, for he was not aware that a dangerous organization with roots worldwide now knew of his existence and the threat he posed to them.
However, unlike the Dark Devil Church, this organization ran much deeper, so it wasn’t hard to determine who could threaten them.
The Hand was now after Kent, and they were using the Middle Finger Assassin Guild as their weapon. Kent would have to be extra careful this time.
Meanwhile, Kent arrived at the hotel with Nara and Lady Lani, who remained quiet throughout the journey.
They just keep staring at him on the journey back to the hotel.

They hadn’t expected to watch a Root Great Sage kill 15 assassins, each at a stage higher than his own. Kent was like a death lord. He casually slaughtered the assassins as if it were a normal thing to do.
"How did you do it?" Lady Lani asked the moment they entered their suite. "How did you kill them using nothing, not even your sword?"
She was asking about the two who died when he used the [Soul Rending Glare]. It was as if he just looked at them, and they fell to their deaths.
"I used a soul attack." Kent didn’t really have the time to hide things from her.
If she stuck around for a while, she would learn most of his secrets, so he might as well save her the shock when she found out in the future.

"But they were all Transcendents while you’re just a Great Sage. At best, you should only be able to knock them unconscious or deal soul damage. Killing them isn’t something a Great Sage should be able to do."
"That’s because I’m not a Great Sage. I’m actually a Root Ascension in soul cultivation." This hit her like a hammer to the soul.
"You are what...!"
Nara giggled, staring at her friend. She had been privileged to have her shocked moment back in the tower, so Kent wasn’t really surprising her.
But Lady Lani was different.
She knew that before one could reach the level of a Kingdom Protector, their soul had to reach the Tier 10 stage.
She had only ever met two people who hadn’t yet reached the Kingdom Protector stage but were at that level.
One was the sect master of the Soul Refining Sect, and the other was the sect master of the Soul Arts Sect.
Today, she met her third, and it was a mere Great Sage.
"Just how old are you?" she asked.
"Don’t worry, Lady Lani, I’m of age, so you won’t be doing anything bad getting freaky with me."
"You... answer the question."
Kent laughed. "I’m 18."
Her world came undone, and even Nara widened her eyes. Kent had to carry them to their beds and tuck them in.

chapters.title: Chapter 438: Second Day of The Pill Master Competition
paragraphs: "Good morning, ladies," Kent greeted, staring at Lady Lani and Nara, who were also doing the same. The night before was shocking; they weren’t prepared for that.
Hearing Kent is only 18 years old but has already achieved the 10th Tier in soul cultivation, they did not see that coming.
They most certainly did not see that coming.
It was like the discovery was a giant hammer used to hit their heads.
So Kent took them to their room to ensure they didn’t collapse on the ground, and now, staring at him, they could only shake their heads and sigh.
"Is there anything more shocking we should know?" Nara asked.
She thought she knew Kent’s most shocking part, but now that she had learned differently, she realized she was wrong.
"Actually, I am also at the Silver Body stage in Body Cultivation," Kent laughed, making the two ladies sigh and shake their heads.
Kent just moved away and prepared for the second day of the competition.
Meanwhile, Lady Lani and Nara could only wonder about many things.
"Just who is this kid?" Lady Lani asked. She looked at Nara. "I never asked how you met him. I met him during the Annual Auction, which I came up with about 50 years ago when you were dead.
He literally made me very rich and ended up offending Evil Bat."
She smiles. Nara just smirked.
"He saved me. He was the one who saved me, but I never expected him to be this monstrous," Nara shook her head.
"I guess worrying about his safety is useless. Someone with a Tier 10 soul strength wouldn’t need our help." She sighed, and after a while, they left the hotel and returned to the Pill Tower.
"I will see you ladies later. Just make sure you enjoy the show," Kent said.
"Are you sure you wouldn’t show your true nature yet? Many would want to know your true identity," Nara asked, having been made aware by Lady Lani that Kent is the Perfect Alchemist.
"No. Getting challenged is the key here. Showing everyone who I am can wait," Kent answered.
"It’s your decision, I guess." They entered, and Kent went to join the 29 remaining contestants. He was the last to arrive, but he wasn’t late.
Since many were disqualified yesterday for being late, they all came early today. Kent ignored the hostile glares coming from all 29 contestants.
Some are hostile because, unlike Kent, they are some of the geniuses known in the field of alchemy.
Kent is known for his battle prowess, so for such a figure to be ranking third in the competition so far doesn’t sit well with them.
It felt like he was looking down on them, and they hated that.
Kent doesn’t care about them. He was more focused on identifying the hostile looks coming from the audience.
’Looks like I will be having trouble on my hands soon,’ he sighs in his heart.
⟪The master has shown everyone he is rich and resourceful. And while the master is not aware, this is a cultivation world where greed is the centerpiece of everything.⟫
⟪They want your treasures, and they are willing to kill you for it. And while it is shameful of them, they wouldn’t stop until they are all dead or they succeed,⟫ Gaia explained.
’Then I will kill every last one of them. I needed their bodies after all.’ He smiled evilly as he felt Annabelle’s hostile gaze land on him.
He looked up and met her gaze. Then, like the annoying grinch he is, he smiled at her, making the young lady clench her fist.
⟪The master should be careful, though. Many dangers in this world can’t be underestimated. You are strong, but now that your targets aren’t dummies,⟫ Gaia advised, and Kent nodded.
He started waiting for another hour before the elder who officiated yesterday’s trials appeared.
He led everyone to a stage where a setup comprising a cauldron, ingredients, and a small scroll, possibly containing the pill formula, was set up.
"Welcome, everyone. We will be starting the second day as promised yesterday with a Tier 3 pill. This stage requires you to concoct the Bone Hardening Pill with a minimum purity of 70%.
You have three portions of the ingredients and 3 hours to finish everything. If you don’t finish within the three hours, you will automatically be disqualified from the subsequent test.
Also, if your purity is below the 70% stage, you will be disqualified.
You are allowed to use any flame provided you have control over it and can effectively use it. Know that only one cauldron is given, so you can only use your own if you break this.
Additionally, if you don’t believe in the cauldron given, you can use yours from the start.

Lastly, I know this is a competition, but you are not allowed to attack your opponent. If you have an issue with them, just challenge them. More tests are coming, and you can use them as the challenge.
Know that you will be disqualified and your pill flame destroyed if you try attacking your opponents." The elder looked at the faces and smiled.
"Sit according to your tags and wait for the start signal."
Kent went and sat behind the third setup in the first row. Annabelle was a few meters on his left, and Lucas was a few meters on his right.
He looked at both of them and smiled.
He wasn’t teasing them because he could tell the Saints were paying attention to him. They never knew his soul strength was higher than theirs, so he was keeping his attention on them.
Today, they will show him what they think of him; thus, he will know what to do afterward.
"Remember, you have only 3 hours to concoct the Bone Hardening Pill," the elder said. "Your time starts now."
The moment the elder said that, everyone picked up the scroll and looked at the recipe, and then, as the elder had said, divided the ingredients into three portions.
A few minutes later, pill flames lit up as the concoction began.

You are strong, but now that your targets aren’t dummies,⟫ Gaia advised, and Kent nodded.
He started waiting for another hour before the elder who officiated yesterday’s trials appeared.
He led everyone to a stage where a setup comprising a cauldron, ingredients, and a small scroll, possibly containing the pill formula, was set up.
"Welcome, everyone.
We will be starting the second day as promised yesterday with a Tier 3 pill.
This stage requires you to concoct the Bone Hardening Pill with a minimum purity of 70%.
You have three portions of the ingredients and 3 hours to finish everything.
If you don’t finish within the three hours, you will automatically be disqualified from the subsequent test.
Also, if your purity is below the 70% stage, you will be disqualified.
You are allowed to use any flame provided you have control over it and can effectively use it.
Know that only one cauldron is given, so you can only use your own if you break this.
Additionally, if you don’t believe in the cauldron given, you can use yours from the start.
Lastly, I know this is a competition, but you are not allowed to attack your opponent.
If you have an issue with them, just challenge them.
More tests are coming, and you can use them as the challenge.
Know that you will be disqualified and your pill flame destroyed if you try attacking your opponents." The elder looked at the faces and smiled.
"Sit according to your tags and wait for the start signal."
Kent went and sat behind the third setup in the first row.
Annabelle was a few meters on his left, and Lucas was a few meters on his right.
He looked at both of them and smiled.
He wasn’t teasing them because he could tell the Saints were paying attention to him.
They never knew his soul strength was higher than theirs, so he was keeping his attention on them.
Today, they will show him what they think of him; thus, he will know what to do afterward.
"Remember, you have only 3 hours to concoct the Bone Hardening Pill," the elder said.
"Your time starts now."
The moment the elder said that, everyone picked up the scroll and looked at the recipe, and then, as the elder had said, divided the ingredients into three portions.
A few minutes later, pill flames lit up as the concoction began.

chapters.title: Chapter 439: First Round, Kent Antics
paragraphs: If it were up to Kent, he would just use the first round of pill making to end the contest. However, because he needed a challenger, he wouldn’t do that.
The process has begun right now, and looking around, he can see that all 29 contestants have started concocting their pills.
Some have already finished extracting some ingredients.
The Bone-Hardening Pill is one of the most commonly used pills on the market. It requires only 7 ingredients to make.
It’s a good pill but easy to make.
However, there is one tricky bit that can affect the purity.
The seven herbs used are ordinary, meaning their essence is limited. Extracting more with loads of impurities will lower the purity of the pill.
However, you are almost done when you extract all the medicinal essence from it. So Kent was waiting to see how many people could do that.
However, he wasn’t just sitting there.

He was using a flame technique called Cauldron Healing Flame Art to prepare the cauldron. This technique has only one use: to heat the cauldron and keep it at any temperature he wanted.𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝔀𝓮𝒃𝙣𝓸𝒗𝒆𝒍.𝙘𝒐𝒎
This way, instead of heating and reheating when he starts extracting the essence, it would take a quarter of the time.
Naturally, nobody, not even the Saints, recognizes his technique, so the ridicule on the faces of his haters started showing.
"I knew it. He is just good at memorizing things; the real alchemy is not for swordsmen," one person said, looking ridiculously in Kent’s direction.
"I know, right? He thought heating the cauldron for an hour would magically create the pill. What a brat."
"The moment I saw him, I knew he was a fake."
"I knew he was just making stuff up. I am even sure he cheated in the first three trials."
"This brat is just shameless. Just look at him; he has no idea what was going on."
"I knew he was a faker. Just look at how he is dressed. Just who dresses like that?"
"His only best qualities are his looks. Aside from his handsome looks, he is just ordinary."
Just like that, the conversation shifted to people just being jealous of Kent’s looks instead of his impeccable control of the flame.
A few recognized this, but they chose to be shameless. However, those being real started to notice that he wasn’t just heating the cauldron.
They could tell he was heating it to a required temperature level.
"Just what technique is that?" Pill Saint Evilyn asked, looking closely at Kent.
"I also don’t get why he is just sitting there and heating the cauldron. However, I notice something, and that has to do with the current state of his cauldron.
The heat level is when one starts extracting the essence from the pill. However, for some reason, despite him still heating it, the temperature isn’t rising or falling.
This control, just who is this kid?"
Pill Saint Barton said, also looking in Kent’s direction.
They are as lost as everyone else.
Forty-six minutes later, a pill smell and a smoky puff came from one direction. Kent turned and looked to his left, only to see Elaine open her cauldron and take out a brown pill.
"Wow, that looks like it has reached the 90% purity level. It might even be higher than that," someone in the audience said.
"Lady Elaine isn’t the top genius for no reason."
Her admirers started singing her praises as she placed the pill in a pill bottle and relaxed in her seat. She subtly turns and looks in Kent’s direction.
On his table, she could see he still has all three portions of the ingredients, meaning he hasn’t started yet.
A small chuckle escaped her lips, making Kent smile in his head.
Five minutes later, Annabelle was also done. She had also retrieved a brown pill that looked like it had crossed the 90% purity level.
Just like Elaine, she also turned and looked at Kent with a ridiculous expression.
And an hour and a half later, all seven geniuses and a few others finished. Kent managed to get all he wanted, so he just sighed and chose to shock them but keep them guessing for a while.
He picked two ingredients and tossed them in the cauldron, causing everyone to gasp. But a second later, ridiculous smiles appeared on their faces.

However, a minute later, their ridiculous smiles vanished when he picked yet another two and tossed them in. This time, they paid attention, and that was when they saw he wasn’t destroying the ingredients.
This caused them to pay more attention to him.
⟪Master, at this pace, your purity level will reduce greatly,⟫ Gaia said.
’That is the plan, Gaia. I just want to be in the second rank and ensure the young lady feels threatened. This way, she will know she has a challenger, and this challenger is not simple.
I reckon she will challenge me after this round.’
⟪I see. Then good luck. But I don’t feel comfortable watching you lower your purity level.⟫
’Me too. It felt like I was going against my beliefs. But it’s just this once because after I become Pill Grandmaster, I wouldn’t play this silly game with anyone.’
⟪Alright, master.⟫
Kent tossed the last ingredient in and extracted the essence. Then he started condensing the pill while burning impurities.
This also shocked the Saints. They knew the best way was to burn impurities and condense, but Kent was doing both at the same time, and he wasn’t even struggling.

’She had a 94% pure pill, and Annabelle was 92%. Since the appraisal will be done for everyone to see, I will just put mine at the 93% stage; however, I will make it look like I made a mistake, which was why I landed there.’
A smile appeared on his face, making everyone start looking more at him. A few minutes into it, he reached his goal and used 30 more minutes to fully condense it.
However, just when he was about to pass the 93rd purity level, he sneezed, causing his flame to fluctuate. This shook the cauldron, and it cracked.
Kent quickly retrieved the pill before the cauldron broke completely.
Many laughed at him, but he just smirked inwardly and started waiting for the appraisal to determine who would progress to the next stage.

chapters.title: Chapter 440: The Appraisal, The Challenge
paragraphs: The sudden explosion of Kent’s cauldron was a ridiculous sight that made many wipe the idea of him being the perfect alchemist from their minds.
Exploding a cauldron on the first trial was just a plain definition of how inexperienced he was. Of course, he managed to finish the pill, but that was beside the point.
Just getting your cauldron to explode in your face as an alchemist is like a swordsman losing hold of their sword in combat.
So they just put him aside and started focusing on some others.
Even the saints were of the same conclusion.
But that was what Kent was after.
He just smiled in his head, stood aside, and started waiting for the appraisal that would determine whether his bait would catch its fish.
After a while, the last of the contestants was done, and the appraisal artifact was brought forward. It was a circular tablet with runic formations on it.
"The appraisal artifact will appraise the pill and tell us the purity percentage of the pill," the elder said, picking up the pill bottle of Elaine.
He opened it and placed the pill on the appraisal artifact.
The moment the pill touched the artifact, it lit up green. Then, from the green, a runic writing of the purity level appeared.
"Congratulations, Pill Master Elaine, your pill appraisal is 94%."

The fans and those coming to suck up to the future Pill Grandmaster and possibly Pill Saint were started praising her. Elaine, on the other hand, just stood to the side, watching everything like it didn’t concern her.
Kent looked at her demeanor and shook his head.
’Her composure is good. I doubt she is arrogant like the rest.’ He may have appraised her higher than the rest of her peers, who were looking disdainfully at him.
The next pill was Annabelle’s.
The appraisal device showed it was a 92% pure pill. This didn’t surprise anyone. They all knew Annabelle was just lagging behind Elaine by a few degrees.
Catching up to her wouldn’t take long, considering that in their last duel, she was lagging by 6% in purity.
More pills were appraised based on the order of completion.𝒻𝓇𝑒𝘦𝘸𝑒𝒷𝓃ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝒸ℴ𝘮
The rest of the geniuses were in the 90% region. None was able to move past Annabelle. Only Lucas managed to reach the 92% range, catching up to Annabelle.
After a while, Kent’s turn came.
In the audience, people started talking
"What purity do you think he will attain?" someone asked his friend in the audience.
"I was really expecting him to prove he is the Perfect Alchemist, but looking at his poor display, getting 80% will be difficult."
"True, I was really hoping he was the Perfect Alchemist; that would have made things much easier."
"I still think he is the Perfect Alchemist," another person said, making everyone turn and look at him.
"I can see your eyes are working well, but come on, what were you seeing when his cauldron exploded?" one person asked disdainfully.
"Maybe instead of talking like an idiot, pay attention to the process next time. You clearly saw the smoke right before the explosion. That means the pill was done before the explosion.
This also means his purity wasn’t affected," said the one who said Kent is the perfect Alchemist. He is a young man who looks like he was well-versed in the field of alchemy.
"Then how do you explain the cauldron exploding part? Also, if he is the Perfect Alchemist, why wasn’t he able to concoct a perfect pill?
Since you’re a know-it-all, why don’t you tell us what happens when a perfect pill is created?"
"That is beside the point. An alchemist can intentionally lower the purity level of a pill, so there is no need to be concerned about that."
"I may not be the best in the field of alchemy, but I know for a fact one thing alchemists hate is intentionally lowering the purity level of a pill.
So stop this nonsense about him being the Perfect Alchemist."
The only question lingering now is whether or not the Perfect Alchemist is present. If he were present, the appraisal wouldn’t even be needed, for a perfect pill emits light when formed.
Kent’s pill was dropped on the appraisal machine, and to everyone’s shock, the pill was 93% pure.
"Though he manages to concoct a 93% pill, that doesn’t prove he is the Perfect Alchemist."
"True, he indeed isn’t. Now, while I don’t want to create any rumors, I hear Pill Master Elaine has a relationship with one of the managers in the Silver Leaf Auction House.
Now, before you all eat me, know that the perfect pills came from one of the managers there. So while I don’t want to sound like an idiot, I believe Elaine is the Perfect Alchemist.
You all saw how she effortlessly concocted the 94% pure pill. I believe she is the Perfect Alchemist." Someone suddenly found a new target.
"You might be onto something here."

"Indeed. The only question is if her master knew about it." They all turned and looked in the direction of Pill Saint Enex; however, looking at the expression on his face, they all wiped that idea from their heads.
Frustration started bubbling up in their minds as they tried to figure out who the Perfect Alchemist was. In the end, after the last appraisal, they paused and decided to wait for the next contest.
Thirty participated in the first trial, but only twenty-two made it to the next round.
"Rest for the next two hours; the next trial will begin after," the elder said, and the twenty-two remaining started moving away to prepare.
Kent decided to go back to his carriage and wait for the time; however, just when he moved two steps, someone stopped before him.
Kent lifted his eyes and met the gaze of Elaine, who was looking coldly at Kent. She wasn’t saying anything; she just stood there, coldly staring at him.
"Hello, you are in my way," Kent said, snapping his fingers before her eyes.
"I challenge you to a duel. Do you dare accept?" Elaine declared, making everyone that is moving suddenly stop in their tracks.

chapters.title: Chapter 441: Who is Elaine
paragraphs: Elaine is a quiet lady.
She grew up in the countryside where she lived with her mother and father. They both are cultivators but they specialise in healing magic.
Growing up, Elaine was surrounded by the gentle scent of herbs and the soft glow of magical flowers. She lived in peace for her life is peace.
Her parents, though not widely known, were respected healers in their region—calm, wise, and always willing to help the sick and injured.
Their home was a humble cottage nestled near a crystal-clear stream that wound through the emerald hills.
Every morning, when the rays hit its surface, it creates a prism of colors that can mesmerize even the color blind.
Birds chirped in the morning, the wind carried the fragrance of blooming wildflowers, and the nights were filled with quiet, comforting silence.
Elaine, being naturally quiet herself, often preferred the company of plants and scrolls over people.

While the other children in the village played and chased spirit beasts through the woods and forests, she could be found crouched in the garden, observing the reaction of moongrass when exposed to her mother’s healing mist, or reading ancient scrolls about the properties of earth-element herbs.
When she turned ten, something shifted within her.
Her mother fell ill—not gravely, but strange enough to make her worry and start to think.
It wasn’t a wound or sickness that normal healing magic could cure.

Elaine watched her father try spell after spell, brew tea after tea, all to little effect. It was the first time Elaine saw the limits of their magic... and the first time she heard the word "alchemy."
A traveling herbalist, who had come for a refill of spirit flowers, suggested a compound made from three specific herbs that didn’t grow in their region.
It wasn’t magic—it was pure alchemical composition, and it worked. Her mother recovered in a matter of days.
Elaine never forgot the moment she realized that alchemy could go where healing spells could not.
From that day forward, she became obsessed.
At thirteen, she began gathering old alchemy manuals from traders and wanderers who passed through the village. She trades flowers and herbs for them.
She built a small lab behind their cottage—just a wooden shack with a fire pit, a few clay pots, and shelves lined with drying herbs. They call her the barefoot lab rat.
But she never really cared about the name given to her.
She was determined to move past just healing magic. She wants to become an Alchemist so that if her parents can’t use their healing magic, she will step in and help with alchemy.
Her early attempts were clumsy—vials exploded, concoctions burned, and her eyebrows were once singed off entirely—but she was undeterred.
Her parents are the type who wouldn’t look down on her. They knew her path was a difficult one, but as good parents, they supported her to the best of her abilities.
At fifteen, she succeeded in creating her first stable pill: a basic Qi Recovery Pill.
It was a minor feat in the grand scheme of cultivation, but for her, it was monumental. She was happy, very happy that she even danced all around her small lab.
Her parents celebrated with her.

She started treating minor injuries in the village, refining her techniques, and even began experimenting with spiritual catalysts—dust of violet orchid, ash from dreamroot bark, and crystals that amplified elemental essence.
She never forgets her roots as a healer, so she tried to mix her healing magic with alchemy. Her success rate wasn’t high, but she was moving toward a bigger picture even without knowing it.
It was during a small regional alchemy gathering, held in the nearby city, that her path crossed with the one who would change her life forever.

Elaine, now seventeen, had traveled there with a basket of her pills to trade for rare ingredients. She wasn’t a participant—just a curious girl from the countryside—but her quietly burning talent didn’t stay hidden for long.
During a public demonstration by a local alchemist, a misstep in the process caused a dangerous backlash in the cauldron.
Panic spread as toxic fumes started rising, but Elaine stepped forward calmly, mixed a neutralizing powder on the spot, and threw it into the cauldron.
The reaction stopped instantly.
That was when Pill Saint Enex noticed her.
He had been there, not as a judge or guest of honor, but in disguise, wandering in search of hidden talents as he often did.
He needed someone he could pass his knowledge to. He was at the peak of this continent, so he needed a disciple. This forced him to travel the four kingdoms in disguise.
That was when he saw Elaine.
He observed her the entire time.
The steady hands, the calm breath, the clear understanding of herbs and their counteracting properties. That kind of intuition couldn’t be taught.
He recognised her talent and thus set his mind to get her as his disciple.
Later that night, as Elaine returned to her inn, she found a letter under the door of her makeshift lab.
It bore the insignia of the Pill Saint’s seal.
"You have the spark. If you wish to fan it into a flame, meet me at sunrise by the eastern gate. —Enex.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝕨𝕖𝗯𝚗𝚘𝕧𝕖𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝕞
And so, her quiet life in the countryside began to shift. Her parents recognised that insignia and knew stopping her would just be them being selfish.

The girl who once sat alone in fields of flowers was now standing at the edge of a vast alchemical path, one that would soon shake the foundations of even the most ancient pill sects in the worlds out there.
However, the moon only blooms at night. When the sun is up, the moon cannot be seen. It was also why a person’s character cannot be determined by their first impression.

sentences.text: Elaine is a quiet lady.
She grew up in the countryside where she lived with her mother and father.
They both are cultivators but they specialise in healing magic.
Growing up, Elaine was surrounded by the gentle scent of herbs and the soft glow of magical flowers.
She lived in peace for her life is peace.
Her parents, though not widely known, were respected healers in their region—calm, wise, and always willing to help the sick and injured.
Their home was a humble cottage nestled near a crystal-clear stream that wound through the emerald hills.
Every morning, when the rays hit its surface, it creates a prism of colors that can mesmerize even the color blind.
Birds chirped in the morning, the wind carried the fragrance of blooming wildflowers, and the nights were filled with quiet, comforting silence.
Elaine, being naturally quiet herself, often preferred the company of plants and scrolls over people.

While the other children in the village played and chased spirit beasts through the woods and forests, she could be found crouched in the garden, observing the reaction of moongrass when exposed to her mother’s healing mist, or reading ancient scrolls about the properties of earth-element herbs.
When she turned ten, something shifted within her.
Her mother fell ill—not gravely, but strange enough to make her worry and start to think.
It wasn’t a wound or sickness that normal healing magic could cure.
Elaine watched her father try spell after spell, brew tea after tea, all to little effect.
It was the first time Elaine saw the limits of their magic... and the first time she heard the word "alchemy."
A traveling herbalist, who had come for a refill of spirit flowers, suggested a compound made from three specific herbs that didn’t grow in their region.
It wasn’t magic—it was pure alchemical composition, and it worked.
Her mother recovered in a matter of days.
Elaine never forgot the moment she realized that alchemy could go where healing spells could not.
From that day forward, she became obsessed.
At thirteen, she began gathering old alchemy manuals from traders and wanderers who passed through the village.
She trades flowers and herbs for them.
She built a small lab behind their cottage—just a wooden shack with a fire pit, a few clay pots, and shelves lined with drying herbs.
They call her the barefoot lab rat.
But she never really cared about the name given to her.
She was determined to move past just healing magic.
She wants to become an Alchemist so that if her parents can’t use their healing magic, she will step in and help with alchemy.
Her early attempts were clumsy—vials exploded, concoctions burned, and her eyebrows were once singed off entirely—but she was undeterred.
Her parents are the type who wouldn’t look down on her.
They knew her path was a difficult one, but as good parents, they supported her to the best of her abilities.
At fifteen, she succeeded in creating her first stable pill: a basic Qi Recovery Pill.
It was a minor feat in the grand scheme of cultivation, but for her, it was monumental.
She was happy, very happy that she even danced all around her small lab.
Her parents celebrated with her.

She started treating minor injuries in the village, refining her techniques, and even began experimenting with spiritual catalysts—dust of violet orchid, ash from dreamroot bark, and crystals that amplified elemental essence.
She never forgets her roots as a healer, so she tried to mix her healing magic with alchemy.
Her success rate wasn’t high, but she was moving toward a bigger picture even without knowing it.
It was during a small regional alchemy gathering, held in the nearby city, that her path crossed with the one who would change her life forever.
Elaine, now seventeen, had traveled there with a basket of her pills to trade for rare ingredients.
She wasn’t a participant—just a curious girl from the countryside—but her quietly burning talent didn’t stay hidden for long.
During a public demonstration by a local alchemist, a misstep in the process caused a dangerous backlash in the cauldron.
Panic spread as toxic fumes started rising, but Elaine stepped forward calmly, mixed a neutralizing powder on the spot, and threw it into the cauldron.
The reaction stopped instantly.
That was when Pill Saint Enex noticed her.
He had been there, not as a judge or guest of honor, but in disguise, wandering in search of hidden talents as he often did.
He needed someone he could pass his knowledge to.
He was at the peak of this continent, so he needed a disciple.
This forced him to travel the four kingdoms in disguise.
That was when he saw Elaine.
He observed her the entire time.
The steady hands, the calm breath, the clear understanding of herbs and their counteracting properties.
That kind of intuition couldn’t be taught.
He recognised her talent and thus set his mind to get her as his disciple.
Later that night, as Elaine returned to her inn, she found a letter under the door of her makeshift lab.
It bore the insignia of the Pill Saint’s seal.
"You have the spark.
If you wish to fan it into a flame, meet me at sunrise by the eastern gate. —Enex.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝕨𝕖𝗯𝚗𝚘𝕧𝕖𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝕞

chapters.title: Chapter 442: The Stakes
paragraphs: Kent, like everyone else, could only look at Elaine.
He was looking forward to her challenge, and when it came, he was rather stunned. But looking at her, he knew her challenge wasn’t that simple.
"Well, are you bold enough to accept my challenge?" she asked again.
"Why should I accept your challenge knowing I will lose?" Kent asked with a chuckle.
"You are the second ranker, only a percentage away from catching up to me. I say we are in the same class," Elaine replied, still looking as cold as ever.
"We all know that your pill could have been more than 94%." Kent wanted to make things fun but Elaine wasn’t buying it.
"So tell me, what are the stakes, and what evil plans do you have in mind, trying to set me up?" Kent smiled, causing the audience and the contestants around to look at Elaine.
"I don’t need anything from you. However, if you lose, you will become my servant for ten years, and within those ten years, you will not touch a cauldron or even a sword.
Your only job will be to serve me."
Her stake was indeed huge, and everyone who heard it turned and looked at Kent. He wasn’t speaking, for he was laughing uncontrollably.
Her demand is rather unusual.
Meanwhile, up in the VIP room, Pill Saint Enex smiled, causing the rest of the Pill Saints to glare at him.
"You bastard, what did you do?" Pill Saint Barton asked with angry eyes.
"What does it look like? Clearly, having him as a servant will mean all his possessions will be my disciple’s to have for the next ten years.

And we all know whatever she has is also mine. So relax, I will be winning this one, but since we are colleagues, I will remember you when I get my hands on his treasures," he said with an evil smile.
"In fact, I only asked her to put the stakes at a year, but ten years is also okay. The brat will die before a year is even over."
"You scheming bastard. You went against all of us and took action on your own. This wasn’t what we agreed on," said Pill Saint Evilyn, the queen of the Athea Kingdom.
Pill Saint Enex just smirked.
"We may be allies when it comes to this brat, but in the grand scheme of things, we all know we fight for our own benefits.
I got my chance today; maybe next time, it will be your turn."
The faces of everyone were rather unpleasant. Even Pill Saint Riva, the poison witch, was ashen.
However, her mood brightened a bit when Pill Saint Barton started laughing. The moment the scheming bastard started laughing, she knew they were back on track.
That laughter said he wasn’t angry anymore; instead, he was ridiculing Pill Saint Enex.
"I received word yesterday that the Evil Sect and the Assassin Guild are coming after the brat and everyone in his life.
This means I can just reach out and let them know after the competition that the brat will be under your care."
"You wouldn’t dare," Pill Saint Enex stood up with his fists clenched.
"Oh, but I will. Just like how you planned on backstabbing us, I also have measures in place," he laughed.

"So what do you think? Unlike you, I will let all of us share the loot equally. We just have to do as we did many years before: we have to get in bed with evil, and our dreams will be fulfilled." His evil smile made the other Pill Saints shudder.
Pill Saint Enex may have crafted the perfect plan with his disciple, but in the end, it was Pill Saint Barton who won.
However, what none of them expected next was the stunt Elaine was about to pull.
"You want me to become your servant for ten years?" Kent asked.
"Yes. Unless, of course, you are willing to reject the challenge, in which case you will be expelled from the rest of the competition. That is the second stake, so pick one."

"I pick the first," Kent smiled. "Then how about I also offer the same stake? If I win, you will become my servant, and just like you offered me, you won’t touch a cauldron or an herb in the ten years you will serve."
"I accept. However, how can I be sure that you won’t run after you lose? I know I wouldn’t, but I don’t trust you, so I need insurance," Elaine asked, making Kent chuckle.
He turned in a certain direction, meeting the gaze of an ordinary-looking man.
"Sword King Shawn, why don’t I disturb you for a while?" Kent called out and smiled.
Everybody turned in the direction he did, and to their shock, the ordinary-looking man smiled and took off his disguise, revealing the face of the swordsman Kent had met at the auction.
"Your perception is indeed admirable. You even managed to see through my perfect disguise," Sword King Shawn smiled.
Not even the Pill Saints saw through his disguise. This caused Pill Saint Enex to panic.𝙛𝓻𝒆𝒆𝒘𝙚𝓫𝙣𝙤𝒗𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
Sword King Shawn vanished and appeared between Kent and Elaine. "Just what are your eyes made of?"
"Let’s say I was fortunate enough to have a fortuitous encounter a while ago that gave me eyes that can see anything," he amplified his tone, making sure everyone heard him.
However, his words only struck chords in the person who knew her suspicions were true.
"What do you need from me? I have decided to do three favors for you since the Spirit Enlightenment Fruit helped me advance my swordsmanship," Sword King Shawn said.

"Then I will cash in the first favor. I want you to enforce the bet. If I lose and choose not to fulfill my end of the bet, you have my permission to do whatever you want to me," Kent said, shocking everyone.
"Do the same for me, Sword King," Elaine also said, making everyone’s blood boil.
The notion that Kent is the Perfect Alchemist returned. However, it wasn’t just that; the rumor that Elaine is also the Perfect Alchemist started to spread.
This made the next round get rowdy. Everyone started whispering, knowing full well that soon, the reveal they’d all been waiting for would come.
"Let it be known that should either of them go against the stakes of the bet, my sword will speak, and that is final."
When a Sword King speaks, there is no doubting it. Not even King has a say after they speak.

chapters.title: Chapter 443: Man With Integrity
paragraphs: The challenge is set, and not even the Pill Saints can stop it.
The moment Kent included Sword King Shawn, their challenge became irreversible. In fact, Kent didn’t know he had just placed the Pill Saints in a tight spot.
Naturally, they started to panic.
Why?
This is because they knew something wasn’t right, and looking at Kent now, they could tell the brat may have tricked them all.
But then again, Pill Saint Enex just doesn’t understand why his disciple will opt for ten years instead of the discussed one year.
Did she perhaps want this outcome from the start?
This was making him question himself. Of course, his mood didn’t escape the eyes of the scheming Barton.
"Are you not feeling well, Enex? It looks like you are sweating," he teased, making sure the backstabbing Pill Saint knew his situation was the perfect karma he could receive.
"At this rate, I will be very happy if that brat is actually the perfect alchemist and he manages to take your disciple from you," Pill Saint Evilyn said with a smirk.
They are all a cabal of scheming bastards, until one of them tried to play smart. But that now looks like he wouldn’t be getting what he wanted.
"Let’s hope that is the case. From what I learned, you will be losing more than just a disciple. I mean, you think we don’t know about your other side?" Pill Saint Riva spoke.
She also seems to want to play her role and make the Pill Saint, who is now having a midlife crisis thanks to his life choices, regret.
They made him regret for a few moments before focusing on the next big plan.
Meanwhile, Kent and Elaine were staring at each other, making sure they sized each other up. Kent held a small smile on his face.
The situation couldn’t be any better than this.
Everybody knew Sword King Shawn was a man of integrity.

He is a man of his word. The fact that he even went as far as killing his own disciple just to uphold justice was enough to tell everyone the second round of the competition will determine the winner.
After the duel, the rest wouldn’t make much sense.
Kent would want to go all out per their expectation, for becoming one’s servant for ten years isn’t something that can be taken lightly.
Elaine wouldn’t hold back either.
"Are you ready to become my servants?" Kent asked with a smile. "Though it wouldn’t be as bad as you think. I won’t abuse my authority over you."
"I am confident in this generation. I am the best, and I believe in my abilities, so be prepared to become my servant, Kent," Elaine spoke.
This is the longest and perhaps the most interaction she had ever had with someone who isn’t her master. So to most, this was a rare sight.
"I might be the perfect alchemist in disguise, you know," Kent smiled.
Elaine looked at him and, as if trying to scoff, she moved away to prepare for the second round, which had already been labeled as Kent and her challenge.
Kent just chuckled and walked away. A few meters away, Sword King Shawn caught up to him, and they walked away together.

Though he clearly showed he was on Kent’s side, or more like he and Kent are familiar with each other, everyone knew he wouldn’t pick a side no matter the outcome of this duel between Kent and Elaine.
So watching them walk away was just a normal sight to many. They thought they just couldn’t understand how someone could be this awesome.
Kent may be a brat, but he has a Sword King on his side. That is enough to tell them he was no ordinary person.
"Are you sure you want to make such a bet?" Sword King Shawn asked Kent, now seated atop the golden carriage.
"I know you have a good handle on your sword, but this is a different world, one where you need to train for years to master pill making.
The lady you are going against isn’t an ordinary person."
Though he doesn’t know Kent much, he has helped him, so he was just making sure he knew what he was getting into.
"Me being beside you now will save you, but should you manage to win the duel, I doubt her master will let things go that easily.
And let me tell you, the Pill Saints are a scheming bunch, so I ask again, are you sure you want this duel to go on?"
Kent smiled.
"Having the disciple of a Pill Saint as my servant doesn’t sound too bad."
Sword King Shawn sighed.
"I guess you should prepare yourself for trouble, though. The outcome of this duel isn’t something simple, and in case you are not aware, the Evil Sect is on the move.
It was also the reason why I came here in the first place. They are trying to trap you in this city and kill you by all means.
I am afraid this time, more than one Sovereign will show up."
Though he is still at the peak of the Transcendent stage, his soul strength has already transcended the 8th Tier, so he is more attuned to the changes in the air.
This caused him to dig into it, and from what he uncovered, it seems a great battle will take place soon. This, of course, made him wonder who the target.
However, without even thinking, he knew Kent was the target.
It all started when he arrived for the pill competition.
Of course, as a Sword King from the Life Path Sword Sect, he must ensure his sect is protected. This means that although Kent helped him greatly, helping him fight them will bring doom on his sect.
This made him only gather as much intel as he could find, and at least give him a head start.
"Looks like some people just choose to court death. I must prepare, then," Kent sighed. He expected this before coming this time.
He knew the transcendent he killed on his way to Vastport City was just the bait set to alert the ones plotting against him.
He was confident he would win regardless.
However, he didn’t expect to hear what comes next.
"A Forest King might be after you."

chapters.title: Chapter 444: Hidden Dangers
paragraphs: Hearing a Forest King might be after him made him alert.
A Forest King is a being akin to a Kingdom Protector, someone sitting at the peak of this world. That was like hearing a god is after him.
"It’s not conclusive, but the chances of that happening are high," Sword King Shawn reaffirms.
"How sure are you?" Kent asked.
"To some extent, I can say very likely. The reason being, you have something they want."
"The Forest King body I purchased at the auction," Kent said.
"Indeed," Sword King Shawn nodded.
"What do you know of the power dynamics of this part of the world?" He went ahead and asked. Kent thought for a moment before answering.
"I know there are four kingdoms, each having a protector who sits at the peak of this world. Aside from that, I know nothing else."
Kent sighs.
Though the enchanted book he received from the enchantress helped him know more of this world, it didn’t show everything. It’s more like it shows what is most known by many.
So since everyone knew of the four kingdom protectors, he managed to know of them too. Of course, he didn’t get their names, mainly because these figures are hidden from most.
"Then you know nothing at all," Sword King Shawn smiled.
"I will tell you what you are sitting in now," he began. "Though there are indeed four protectors, they are not the strongest of this continent.
In fact, the strongest of this continent are not we humans but the spirit beasts. Of course, this will puzzle you, but there are spirit beasts among us, and they are all around us.
You wouldn’t understand much now, mainly because on this continent, the concept of other races is still not fully known.
But if you visit the other continents, you will know that the spirit beasts are just like we humans.
So on this continent, or even this world, the spirit beasts are the strongest. I met them, and that is why I am this confident.
However, they can’t invade us simply because of a rule prohibiting them.
They have their own kingdoms, with one of such kingdoms being the Wild Forest. Now, before I scare you, know that we have four forests on this continent.

The Wild Forest, the Dark Forest, the Demon Mountains, and the Twisting Vine Forest. Of these four, the Wild Forest is the biggest of them all, simply because it houses seven Forest Kings, while the others only have one.
From what I know, these seven Forest Kings are each at the peak, and when I say the peak, they are at Level 9 Core Formation.
This made them the strongest in the entire world. However, this is also the reason why you are in grave danger.

From the reports I received, the Forest King in your possession isn’t one of the seven but more like a hidden trump card of the Mountain Flame Tiger, one of the strongest beasts on this continent and perhaps the entire world.
It was killed by a rival Forest King, and even its body was sold to the humans. You may be wondering why that was done and who would have done it.
The answer to this question is the other races.
I don’t know for sure which of them, but I am confident it’s the elves, for the humans, and they are natural enemies.
This is why whenever we meet at the ancient battlefield of Parting, we either kill each other or ignore one another.
But while we humans aren’t that petty, the elves are greedy and ambitious.
They are breaking the rules that prevent the spirit beasts from attacking us, and you may be the only thing standing between them."
Kent was rather puzzled hearing that.
He appeared on this continent less than a year ago, so how the hell did he become the block that is preventing this battle from happening?
"You bought something that belongs to the beasts, and as such, you broke a rule. Of course, you weren’t the one who killed it, but you bought it.
This means you have something you shouldn’t have.
I only found out about this a few days ago. Apparently, the rule preventing the beasts from invading was a forbidden formation left behind by the previous emperor.
He was one of the top cultivators who vanished after the ancient battlefield of Parting.
This formation held the spirit beasts back all these years. However, that will be changing soon. The body now in your possession may be the key to breaking this formation.
This made this much more difficult, for if what I know is the case, your life has been linked to the beast somehow, and as such, the moment you die, the formation will become undone."
"In other words, the death of the Forest King wasn’t by accident," Kent said.
"Indeed, this also means you bought a forbidden item. However, you didn’t die after the evil sect attacked, and as such, they will try again until your blood is spilled.
This also means the Evil Sect isn’t acting alone. I don’t know much on that front though, but after pulling some strings, I can say you are their target.
The Beasts, Elves, and even humans are after you."
A couple of meters from Kent and Sword King Shawn, a small dark bird was perched atop a wooden structure, overhearing their conversation.
Hundreds of miles away, Kingdom Protector Vari sighed.

"Now you know, Kent, what will be your next move? Either way, you wouldn’t be able to walk away from this now, so just what are you going to do next?" She took another sigh and continued with her cultivation.
Back in Vastport City.

"So a different race, possibly the elves, chose to ally with the beasts of this continent and invade us by making us have something they possess, and in doing so, create some form of connection that now links my life to their formation.
Meaning the only thing standing in their way is me. Am I making sense?" Kent asked.
"Yes. They want you dead, from what I know."
"Then why do they want to rule over humans?"
For these people to go the extra mile means they are after something. It wouldn’t be as simple as just wanting to become the supreme rulers of the humans.
"That is the thing; nobody knows what they are after, at least I don’t. But I can make a guess, and that is because on the ancient battlefield of Parting.
The humans have captured a region that contains a rare mineral we’ve been protecting for years already.
And since the Forest Kings can’t enter unless the formation is down, this can only mean that the moment they gain control over the four kingdoms, everything will be theirs."
"Damn, that is one conspiracy right there." Kent smiled. "Looks like the Hand and the Dark Devil Church can rest for now; I have beasts and elves to put in their place first.
Looks like visiting the other continent is a must now. I must get to know them at least before I put them in their place."
"Did you just say the Hand?"
This time, it was Sword King Shawn who was shocked.

chapters.title: Chapter 445: Start of the Second Round
paragraphs: Some secrets are better left alone.
These secrets will make you wonder if there are indeed rules in this world.
Sword King Shawn once encountered a mysterious group of individuals in the ancient battlefield of Parting who called themselves The Hand.
It was when he was a mere Sword Sage.
He was so terrified that he fled and did not stop running for a month.

That was the scariest he had ever been because he witnessed how these people slaughtered a group of adventurers from one demon state, and from what he managed to gather before he was exposed, they are everywhere.
This made him alert; for years, he has always been alert.
When he returned to the human continent, he tried gathering information on them but came out empty-handed. Years have passed, yet he hasn’t heard the name "The Hand" come out of anyone’s mouth...
...until today, when he heard Kent call it.

"We must have a good sit-down, Sword King. I can tell we have a lot to discuss." Kent knew the name triggered him, and if he were to get into it now, they wouldn’t be done before the second round of pill-making.
He could tell the Sword King had something blocking him. Naturally, the name ’The Hand’ triggered him, making Kent, who has Mind Weaver in his head, reveal everything to him.
’Looks like he will need my help again, ’ Kent told himself. But he wasn’t about to get into it just yet.
He did not want to stand in public and talk about these people.
Sword King Shawn understood that, so he didn’t make life too difficult for Kent.
"Then after the competition, we will have a sit-down," he said before vanishing from sight. Kent sighed and lay on the carriage like he hadn’t just been informed his life was in danger.
After a while, he turned and looked at the black bird and smiled, "Big sister, I thought you didn’t deal with the stuff of us mortals."
His smile was teasing, making the beautiful Kingdom Protector, now watching and hearing all he said through the bird, clench her fist.
It was like getting caught while sneaking to steal fish from the soup.
"No need to worry, big sister. I knew of this scheme long before buying the Forest King’s body. The question now is what I will do with them," Kent smiled again.
Even the being sitting at the peak of this world shuddered watching that smile.
There was just something about that smile that made her shudder.
Kent, of course, didn’t know that, but his inner evil, which he never knew was there, started to surface, and right now, even his ladies would be scared by the look on his face.
Since he started recovering Jest’s memories, strange personalities seem to surface every now and then. It felt like he was calling out to his past whenever an aligning situation surfaced.
Right now, a rather evil or perhaps wicked smile appeared on his face.
But it vanished, and a playful smile appeared instead, making the black bird glare at him.
He continued to sleep on the carriage, waiting for the second round to resume. He wasn’t really concerned about the forest king and whatnot.
Naturally, Gaia identified the spell on the body of the Forest King he had bought. The spell was meant to link his life to the formation, which means that the moment he died, the formation would end.
However, there was something else that made him applaud the schemers.
The token that came with the Forest King’s body, which was meant to give him a free pass for a week inside the wild forest, even the deepest part, was actually a tracking token.
This would allow whoever was after him to track his location. If Kent had naively entered the forest, he would have become a meal served on a silver platter to the beasts.
It wasn’t a free pass but a means to an end.
Thankfully, Gaia identified all this, and even Akira neutralized the spell that latched onto his soul. Not that it would have worked, considering he is immune to soul attacks.
The only thing he was waiting for now was when the true horrors behind this scheme would appear.
He knew The Hand had something to do with it, one way or another.
He had no idea what, but one of these days, he would find out.
Hopefully, by then, he would be ready.
Two hours later, the second round of the pill concoction trial began. Kent went back inside, and they were given new tags like before.
However, he and Elaine were set up on a different platform.
Elaine is, at the moment, the first ranker, with Kent being the second. They are on a different platform.
Then again, this was a special duel between them, so being on the same platform was only natural in this aspect.
After everyone had settled down, Kent looked at her, and she stared back.
"Hope you said goodbyes to your master; there won’t be a second chance for that." His smile was both teasing and infuriating.
"Worry about yourself, Kent." Elaine wanted to fire back like he did, but she isn’t good with words, so she knew Kent would win in that department regardless of how hard she tried.
"Annabelle would have been a good sport; too bad she’s a spoiled brat who only knows how to hate without any valid reason."
When Annabelle heard her name, she clenched her fist, but before she could fire back, her master spoke to her telepathically, stopping her.
Kent laughed but made sure his focus remained on the Pill Saints, who were now paying even more attention to him.
This is the moment their plans will be put in disarray if the plans they have in mind weren’t the ones that come out after the duel.
They will know soon.
"Everyone, welcome to the second round of the Pill Master competition. This time, the setup has been changed slightly due to the duel we always see happening in Pill Master competitions.
This time, the first and second rankers from the first round will compete against each other. The winner takes the loser as a servant for ten years.
Now, before you all think it won’t be enforced, know that Sword King Shawn is overseeing this duel and will ensure the bet is fulfilled, regardless of the background of the two of them.
We don’t want to waste anyone’s time, so you two are required to say something to each other before we start, as we always do.

chapters.title: Chapter 446: The Duel
paragraphs: Elaine stared at Kent’s face, looking for the words to say, but in the end, she only managed to utter a single line.
"May the best Alchemist win."
The audience actually received those words well, and they started cheering for her. Her unspoken nature was just too cute, making her look much more lively yet hidden.
But after her cheering died down, Kent smiled and shook his head.

"A wise man once said," Kent paused, his gaze drifting toward his opponent, "alchemy isn’t about winning. It’s about healing, about understanding the balance between what is broken and what can be made whole."
The crowd quieted as his voice carried across the space, clear and calm. Even the other competitors momentarily held their breath, sensing something different in his tone.
Elaine blinked, surprised by the sudden weight of his words. She hadn’t expected a reply like that—not from Kent.
Naturally, everyone expected some shameless words. But it’s safe to say he surprised them all, and that made them wonder what he was up to.
"But," he continued, eyes locking with hers again, "if it comes down to winning... then let’s both aim for it with everything we’ve got."
A quiet murmur rippled through the audience, impressed by his resolve. Then, a slow but steady round of applause followed, growing louder with each second.
Kent, of course, had to make it shameless, so he stood up and gave gentle bows like the elegant alchemist he was.
Naturally, this didn’t sit right with the Pill Saints. Getting this much love from people who were meant to hate him wasn’t what they were aiming for.
But that could wait for now. Kent had won this round, and they could only frown in peace.
"The second round will be slightly difficult," the elder began. "The pill for the second round is the Bone Tempering Pill."
Gasps rippled across the space when they heard the name of the pill the contestants will be making.
The first round was the Bone Hardening Pill, which is the easiest to make. But the Bone Tempering Pill isn’t one that can easily be made.
The reason being, unlike the Bone Hardening Pill, which is a 7-ingredient pill, the Bone Tempering Pill is a 14-ingredient pill and one of the top Tier 3 pills every pill master will struggle with.
This is where one is required to have high spiritual energy; otherwise, the pill wouldn’t finish concocting, and you will run out.
The elder smiled.
"Of course, while the pill is hard to make, you have three portions of the ingredients, so this means third time’s the charm.
Again, before you think you will run trials before focusing on the real thing, know that you only have three hours.
This means you will only have an hour of trial session since the required time for this pill is mostly within the second hour.
Also, the passing purity level is now 85%. Anything below that won’t be accepted.
Good luck, and may the best alchemist win."

The moment the elder ended his speech, everyone rushed to start concocting, except Kent. He just sat there. There wasn’t even a cauldron on his table, simply because he destroyed the first one in the first round.
However, nobody said anything. He just sat there and continued to stare at Elaine, who was among the 21 who started working on their pill.
She divided the ingredients and lit her pill flame within 10 minutes, starting to heat the cauldron.
She had a yellow pill flame, which, if its source were traced, would be a flame from a rare spirit beast called the Winding Flame Bat.
It’s a good flame that requires less spiritual qi to harness.
Since the beast it came from has both the wind and flame elements, the flame has some traces of the wind element in it, making harnessing it much easier.
But that doesn’t mean she can casually use it without much attention to her control.
Naturally, Kent was impressed with her handling of the flame until she started extracting the second ingredient; that was when he noticed she wasn’t really that good.
It was just that she made sure her pill flame didn’t suddenly fluctuate, which in that case would destroy her process.
But that is admirable at best.

’She is good, but she can be better with the right techniques,’ Kent said to himself, considering he had such good techniques in the hundreds and had mastered them since they all just came naturally to him.
It was strange, but he wasn’t complaining.
An hour was almost nearing, yet Kent was still there watching his opponent. Naturally, Kent was doing something that would shock everyone but could also go against him if his ego got the best of him.
When the first hour of the three-hour duration was reached, many started talking about the stunt he was pulling.
"I am confused right now. Is he perhaps forfeiting the duel, knowing he will lose?" someone asked.
"Maybe he doesn’t know the recipe. I noticed there are three wrong ingredients in the ones provided. Maybe he doesn’t know which ones to use."
"I think so, too. Perhaps he doesn’t know what to do with them, so he just wants to copy from Elaine."
Human nature is flawed in this aspect.
Just an hour ago, they were applauding him, and now he was being branded a thief. That was just like seeing him as a saint and a devil in the same body.
Time went by, and before long, two hours had passed, leaving only an hour more.
Elaine was done extracting the pill and was even burning impurities and forming the pill.
However, not everyone managed to get their luck.
Over ten contestants burned two portions of their ingredients, automatically disqualifying themselves.
Even some of the seven geniuses were struggling.
However, they didn’t wash out, considering they managed to form the pill.
However, they were not confident in their abilities to surpass 85% purity or even reach it.
"Puff."
A dark smoke came from Elaine’s cauldron, accompanied by the smell of a pill.
"She succeeded in making the pill," one person from the audience said, prompting everyone to clap for her.𝕗𝚛𝚎𝚎𝐰𝗲𝗯𝗻𝚘𝚟𝚎𝗹.𝕔𝐨𝕞
Even Kent wasn’t an exception. He was clapping, but he had his own intentions in mind.
She retrieved the pill and placed it in her pill bottle.
"92% pure, not bad at all," Kent said, making Elaine turn and look at him.
"Have you given up, considering you have less than 50 minutes?" she asked disappointedly. It seemed she didn’t like seeing her opponent not doing anything.
It felt like a plan she had in mind was getting destroyed, and she didn’t want that.
"You haven’t given up, have you?" She asked again.
Kent smiled. "Actually, I was waiting for you to finish so that I could borrow your cauldron."
